questions.q: What did the Beginner tier of this capstone already build?
options: A tested `customers` mart staged from the real jaffle_shop `raw_customers` seed data, enriched with order history
A fully built Power BI report with every page Finance and Ops need
An incremental orders model with is_incremental() already in place
A Snowflake warehouse with no dbt project yet
questions.explain: The Beginner project's deliverable was a tested customers mart — this capstone now builds the orders analytics layer on top of it.

questions.q: What does Finance specifically need from this project?
options: A list of every customer's email address
A trustworthy revenue number, by day and by payment method, that is stable across repeat pulls
A dashboard showing server CPU usage
A count of orders by status
questions.explain: Finance's ask is about reliable revenue reporting — a number that doesn't move unexpectedly between pulls.

options: A list of all Snowflake warehouses
A revenue total by payment method
A count of orders broken out by status (placed, shipped, completed, returned)
A customer loyalty score
questions.explain: Ops wants order-status tracking: how many orders sit in each status, to spot where orders are piling up.

questions.q: What real source table do both Finance's and Ops's requests trace back to?
options: `raw_payments`
`raw_orders`
A brand-new table that doesn't exist yet
`raw_customers`
questions.explain: Both the revenue view (Finance) and the status-count view (Ops) are different views over the same raw_orders table.

questions.q: What fact about `raw_orders` in this scenario matters most for the rest of the chapter?
options: It only contains orders from a single customer
It is a view, not a table, so it can't be queried directly
It grows with new rows every day the shop is open, which eventually makes a full-reprocess model too slow
It has no `status` column
questions.explain: Unlike a static seed file, this raw_orders grows daily — the real, concrete reason an incremental model becomes worth building later in the chapter.
